marrow__ANAT_CH12_Q015.takeaway: Smooth muscle is unstriated and made of spindle-shaped myocytes with a central elongated nucleus.
marrow__ANAT_CH12_Q015.displayText:
Smooth muscle consists of spindle-shaped myocytes. Smooth muscles are specialized for slow, steady contraction under the influence of autonomic nerves and various hormones. They are also called visceral muscles and are a major component of blood vessels and the digestive, respiratory, urinary and reproductive tracts.

On microscopy, smooth muscle can be identified by:
• In longitudinal section, the spindle-shaped muscle cells are elongated, tapering and unstriated, with a centrally placed elongated nucleus.
• In transverse section, the spindle-shaped cells are cut at different places along their length and therefore appear as a group of cells with different shapes and sizes. A nucleus is seen only in cells cut through the center.

rationales.a: Skeletal muscle fibers are long, cylindrical and striated, with multiple peripheral nuclei; they are not spindle-shaped myocytes.
rationales.c: Cardiac myocytes are striated and branched, usually with a centrally placed nucleus and intercalated discs; they are not spindle-shaped smooth-muscle cells.
rationales.d: Striated muscle includes skeletal and cardiac muscle, both of which have cross-striations; spindle-shaped unstriated myocytes identify smooth muscle.
